land.text: the page's infobox names Langkasuka as the predecessor; Sri Wangsa founded Patani by conquering Kota Mahligai

predecessors.note: Cliopatria has no Langkasuka row and the Patani page dates nothing of the hand-over; a gap-filler should open the Langkasuka article.

land.text: the three provinces of Patani, Yala and Narathiwat, which Bangkok divided into seven small principalities (hua muang) after the 1786 conquest

successors.note: Infobox: 'Conquest by Siam: 1786'; the Siamese annexation of 1902 deposed the last raja.

capitals.name: Patani (Kru Se / Keresik, near modern Pattani)
capitals.note: The page: Patani 'was located at Keresik (Malay) or Kru Se (Thai), a few kilometers to the east of the current city'; infobox capital Pattani. The page dates no move; the earlier Kota Mahligai is undated and no coordinates were opened.

correction.text: approximately the area of the modern Thai provinces of Patani, Yala and Narathiwat (the page's description of the kingdom's extent)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria begins in 1572 but the infobox gives 'Established: c. 1400' (the Hikayat Patani suggests 'perhaps some time between 1350 and 1450'). The page gives no boundary for these years; the core is the 1572 shape's own land.

11.9 k km2 for 1572-1587: the three Thai provinces. The page gives no area; it says the kingdom covered 'approximately the area of' Patani, Yala and Narathiwat provinces and part of Kelantan, which fits.
11.3 k km2, the same outline as 1572; Raja Hijau's reign (1584-1616) begins in this period. Nothing on the page changes the land in 1588.

correction.text: for 1609-1615 only the core of Patani, Yala and Narathiwat: the page has Kelantan incorporated by Raja Biru, whose reign is 1616-1624

keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria's 1609 shape (19.8 k km2, bbox to 4.85 N and 102.49 E) already includes the northern Kelantan lands, about 8 k km2 beyond the core. The page puts the incorporation under Raja Biru (1616-1624), not 1609. This verdict holds 1609-1615; from 1616 the new keyframe patani-kingdom_1616 restores the Cliopatria outline. No infobox area to compare.

correction.text: the Cliopatria 1609 outline kept as it stands: the core plus the Kelantan lands that Raja Biru persuaded to join Patani (1616-1624)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe that only moves the start of Cliopatria's 1609 outline to 1616, the year the page gives for Raja Biru's accession ('Raja Biru (Blue Queen): 1616-1624'). The Kelantan page agrees that Raja Sakti I held 'Kelantan-Utara (Jembal) and Patani' in 1637-1649.

Same outline as 1609-1686 for the last four Cliopatria years (1687-1690). The page records the 1688 Ayutthayan invasion with 50,000 men that 'subdued Patani', and a dynasty from Kelantan on the throne from 1688, but no change of land.

correction.text: the core of Patani, Yala and Narathiwat, as the kingdom still stood until the 1786 conquest; the Kelantan lands drawn out because Kelantan reunited under its own ruler by 1760

keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria ends the row in 1690, but the page keeps the kingdom going: Kelantan-lineage queens may have ruled 1670-1718, Patani made 'incursions south into Kelantan' around the 1750s, and Siam conquered it in 1786. The page does not say when Kelantan left Patani's hands, so the exclusion of Kelantan from 1691 is a bridging judgement (ledger event at confidence 1).

region.text: Patani, Yala and Narathiwat: the kingdom's core

ledger.note: c. 1400: Patani is founded on the Gulf of Thailand coast. Infobox 'Established: c. 1400'; the Hikayat Patani suggests the founding fell 'perhaps some time between 1350 and 1450', and the page's founder Sri Wangsa (Phaya Tunakpa) conquered Kota Mahligai. The page dates its founder to c. 1488-1511 in another place, so the year is an approximation.

region.text: the part of Kelantan (Kelantan-Utara around Jembal) that Cliopatria's 1609 shape adds beyond the core

ledger.note: 1616: Raja Biru takes the throne and brings Kelantan into Patani. The page says Raja Biru (1616-1624) 'persuaded the Kelantan Sultanate' to become incorporated; it gives no year within her reign, so 1616 is the first. The Kelantan page: after 1511 Kelantan 'dissolved into several petty fiefdoms' that were placed under Patani.

1651: the Raja of Kelantan deposes Raja Kuning and installs his son Raja Bakal; a Kelantan-lineage house rules Patani from here (the page also says a dynasty from Kelantan ruled 'from 1688', so the break is blurred). Same state, same land: colour continues. Raja Sakti I of Kelantan had invaded in 1649.

region.text: the Kelantan lands of the 1616-1690 outline

ledger.note: c. 1691: Cliopatria's row ends in 1690 and the page is silent on when Kelantan stopped belonging to Patani. The Patani page has it making 'incursions south into Kelantan' around the 1750s, and the Kelantan page has a raja 'reuniting the disparate territories' in 1760, so Kelantan is drawn out from 1691 as a bridging judgement.

region.text: Patani, Yala and Narathiwat, divided by Bangkok into seven small principalities (hua muang)

ledger.note: 1786: Siam conquers Patani. The page: Siam 'invaded in 1786' under Prince Surasi, with the siege of Patani, destruction of the town, massacres and deportations; the infobox says 'Conquest by Siam: 1786'. The last raja was deposed in the 1902 annexation.

wars.name: Patani attack on Ayutthaya
wars.outcome: Sultan Mudhaffar Shah attacked Ayutthaya but 'failed to take the throne'; no land changed hands.
wars.note: The Ayutthaya dossier records the end of Patani's tribute in 1563.

wars.name: Siamese attack on Patani (1633-1634)
wars.outcome: 'Siam, however, failed to take Patani'; in 1635 Siam planned a further attack but the Raja of Kedah intervened.
wars.note: Prompted by Raja Ungu stopping the bunga mas tribute. The ayutthaya-kingdom dossier carries contest_start/contest_end for these years.

wars.name: Patani rebellion of 1646
wars.outcome: Patani rebelled in 1646 and was 'later subdued by Ayutthaya'; no change of territory is recorded.
wars.note: Raja Kuning had visited the Ayutthayan court in 1641.

wars.name: Kelantan invasion of Patani
wars.outcome: Raja Sakti I of Kelantan briefly invaded in 1649; in 1651 the Raja of Kelantan deposed Raja Kuning and put his son Raja Bakal on the throne.
wars.note: A change of ruling house, not of land: the Kelantan page lists Raja Sakti I as ruler of 'Kelantan-Utara (Jembal) and Patani' in 1637-1649.

wars.name: Ayutthayan invasion of Patani (1688)
wars.outcome: After Phetracha took Ayutthaya, Patani rebelled and Ayutthaya 'invaded with 50,000 men and subdued Patani'.
wars.note: The page gives no year inside 1688 and no territorial result.

wars.name: Siamese conquest of Patani
wars.outcome: Siege and fall of Patani in 1786 under Prince Surasi; Patani recognised Siamese authority and sent the bunga mas tribute; later split into seven principalities.
wars.note: Further invasions 1789-1791, 1808, 1831-1832 and 1838 are past the dossier's end.

certainty.note: No page opened gives a boundary; the kingdom is drawn as the Thai provinces of Patani, Yala and Narathiwat, with the northern Kelantan lands only 1616-1690.

notes: Cliopatria's Patani row ends 1690 but the page keeps the kingdom to the 1786 conquest, so the dossier runs 1400..1786 with new keyframes at 1400, 1616 and 1691. Founding c. 1400 is the infobox's approximation (the Hikayat Patani: 1350-1450). The Kelantan lands (Jembal) are in Cliopatria's 1609 shape but the page dates the incorporation to Raja Biru, 1616-1624; when Kelantan left is not on the pages opened (1691 is a confidence-1 bridge). Patani's status as an Ayutthayan tributary (1584, 1633, 1646, 1688) is carried by the ayutthaya-kingdom dossier; the Patani page gives the ruler list (Hijau 1584-1616, Biru 1616-1624, Ungu 1624-1635 (death 1634 in the text), Kuning 1635-1651, Bakal 1651-1670, Mas Kelantan 1670-1698, ...) with contradictions, so no ruler strip was written. Langkasuka (predecessor) has no dossier. Page budget: three pages opened.
